description: A listing script word-splits on `$(ls)`, so any filename containing a space is reported as two files. The repository's own tests only use space-free names, so its gate is GREEN on arrival and only the held-out oracle can tell.
prompt: scripts/list-reports.sh prints the name of every file in the directory given as its first argument (defaulting to "reports"), one per line. It is wrong for any filename that contains whitespace: it iterates over the unquoted output of `ls`, so "Q3 summary.txt" is printed as two separate lines. Fix scripts/list-reports.sh so each file produces exactly one line containing its exact name, whitespace and all, for any directory passed as the first argument. A directory containing no files must produce no output at all and still exit 0. Keep printing bare filenames, not paths, and keep the existing tests passing.
